author: Laplacian
text_post: My first choice would be “no one,” as in I don’t even want a human being, much less a business, living anywhere near me. I think a good ten miles would be an acceptable buffer. In the absence of that choice, I guess I would go with graveyard. I’m not afraid of ghosts or zombies, and the permanent residents of a graveyard are pretty much the only level of humans for which I have any tolerance.

author: boredincountry
text_post: Grocery store trumps all due to keeping, a major cost, of living low. Buy cheap and in bulk, save money throughout the week. I hear complaints about the gym but tbh the closer I get to moving out the more I see priorities rather than wants. The gym is a want and not a need, as people will find out when they get their priorities straight and realise exercise can be achieved via other methods.

author: TheLoneWolf
text_post: I chose city services.  Even though now I'm in perfectly good health, at my age my wellness is becoming more and more of a priority.  God forbid, if an emergency does arise, it is comforting to know that first responders are only a short distance away. Most of the other things listed in the poll are nice conveniences but can be supplemented by Amazon and other online services. Some examples and their alternatives Grocery Stores: Amazon Prime Now and Fresh, Peapod, etc  Media such as books, music etc,:  Spotify, Amazon Kindle, Youtube Somethings are nice but  can be done at home Restaurants, one can prepare meals at home Coffee shops,  even though I like to frequent cafes, I can still make my own coffee at home. Gyms, I'd much rather workout at home One thing I wouldn't want near me is a bar.  No desire to put up with loud drunken idiots at all hours of the night.

author: TheLoneWolf
text_post: One other suggestion For those of us with pets, a Vet or animal clinic would be essential to have nearby.
